Can we schedule a 30-min call next week to review a concrete sizing proposal? Ideally someone from engineering who can speak to latency/kv-cache tradeoffs joins.

Subject: Re: Commit reconciliation and GPUs for renewal

Thanks — dug into the CSV and ran it against our serving telemetry. Quick summary (high level):

- Utilization pattern: median utilization across the committed pool is ~72%, but sustained 95th-percentile bursts hit ~1.6x the baseline for multi-hour windows on weekdays.
- Workload characteristics: 60% of token volume comes from personalization queries with average context length 1,200 tokens; KV-cache reuse is moderate (~40% hit rate).
- Inference cost model: with current model variant (redwood-rlhf-large), a single A100 equivalent supports ~1.5 rps at your average latency target; burst math below.

Sizing options (trade-offs):
1) Incremental tranche (fastest): +4 A100 equiv. This covers typical peaks and avoids immediate throttling. Estimates: +~$12k/mo incremental committed spend, reduces throttling events by ~70%.
2) Phased scale (recommended): start with +2 A100 now, measure 30 days, then add +6 if sustained. This reduces initial OPEX hit and lets us validate prefix caching improvements.
3) Full add (aggressive): +10 A100 to fully head off future growth — higher commit discount but larger capital commitment.

Operational notes:
- We can enable a short-term burst pool (non-committed) for immediate headroom while the addendum processes; burst pool cost is variable but avoids changing the commit mid-cycle.
- If BrightCart can accept a 30-day measurement window, we’ll instrument per-route token-level cost and provide a post-trial recommendation.

I attached a simple proposed addendum (proposed_commit_addendum.pdf) with numbers and a timeline for rollout, plus a link to the utilization dashboard.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com
Attachment: proposed_commit_addendum.pdf (PDF, 120 KB)
Related link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1u-sample-util-dashboard
From: Elena Martinez <elena@brightcart.com>

Subject: Re: Commit reconciliation and GPUs for renewal

Neha / Dev / Marissa —

Thanks for the thorough options and the addendum. Procurement reviewed the PDF and prefers the phased scale approach (option 2) to limit near-term spend. Their ask: start with a +2 A100 committed tranche immediately, enable a 30-day measurement with the burst pool enabled for emergency headroom, and then move to +8 more (total +10) by Feb 1 if metrics justify it.

Procurement notes: we’ll need an amendment that includes the tranche schedule, a DocuSign link, and confirmation of rollback/fallback policies in case we see regression. Can you put together a mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones (instrumentation, measurement gates, trigger thresholds) and a procurement-friendly cost table?

We can sign the initial +2 tranche addendum this week if you can turn around the DocuSign and MAP.

Best,
Elena Martinez
Head of ML Platform — BrightCart
